title: Stage 0 gate test

video.title: Number of alphabets in Samskritam
video.focus: How the letters are grouped and counted: the vowels, the consonants, and the two add-on sounds (anusvara and visarga).

recap: Your Day 12 answers didn't come in, so here's a quick warm-up on Gita 2.47. W1: split कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते into 4 words. W2: in मा फलेषु, does मा mean (a) always (b) not, never (c) mother? W3: roughly translate मा फलेषु कदाचन.
idea: Today is the **gate test** for Stage 0, the end of the sounds-and-script part of the course. If you score 8 out of 10, you're ready for Stage 1 (sentences and grammar). If you score less, that's fine: we go back over the weak spots first.

Video note: different books count the letters differently, and that's normal. Two things to remember: क्ष त्र ज्ञ, which Hindi charts add at the end, are **conjuncts** (two consonants joined), not extra letters. And अं अः are not vowels.
Read each line aloud with the audio. Tick it off if you can do it without looking.
- All 13 vowels, holding the long ones (आ ई ऊ ॠ ए ऐ ओ औ) for two beats
- Final अ is spoken: राम is rāma, not 'Ram'
- Anusvara ं turns into the nasal of the next consonant's row: संस्कृतम् = sa**n**skṛtam
- Visarga ः at a pause gives a soft h plus an echo of the vowel: रामः = rāmaha
- Aspirated vs plain: क/ख, त/थ, प/फ
- Retroflex ट-row (tongue curled back) vs dental त-row (tongue on the teeth)
- श, ष and स are three different sounds; व is a soft v/w
- ज्ञ = j + ñ (jñ), क्ष = k + ṣ (kṣ)
- Heavy syllables (long vowel, or a vowel followed by ं, ः or two consonants) get two beats
Cover one side and write the other: कृष्णः = kṛṣṇaḥ, ज्ञानम् = jñānam, शान्तिः = śāntiḥ.

sayAloud.iast: karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana
sayAloud.meaning: Your right is to action alone, never to its fruits. (Gita 2.47)

quiz.q: How many vowels does Sanskrit have?
quiz.why: अ आ इ ई उ ऊ ऋ ॠ ऌ ए ऐ ओ औ. अं and अः are not vowels.
ऋ = ṛ, ष = ṣ, ण = ṇ, visarga = ḥ.
jñ is the conjunct ज्ञ; the final m takes a virama: म्.

quiz.q: In शङ्खः, which row does ङ् belong to?
quiz.why: ङ is the nasal of the क-row, so it comes before ख.

quiz.q: Which letter is retroflex (said with the tongue curled back)?
quiz.why: ट is from the ट-row (retroflex); त and थ are dental.
क्ष = क् + ष, so it is kṣa.

quiz.q: How is the visarga in रामः said at the end of a sentence?
options: A soft h with an echo of the vowel: rāmaha
quiz.why: At a pause the visarga is a breathy h that echoes the vowel before it.

quiz.q: In कर्म (kar-ma), the first syllable is:
quiz.why: Its vowel is followed by two consonants (r + m), so it is heavy.
Visarga before त becomes स्: नमस्ते.

quiz.q: In सोऽहम्, what does ऽ (avagraha) show?
quiz.why: सः + अहम् → सो + (अ)हम्; the avagraha marks the missing अ.
